source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade BIOS firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade BIOS firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + BIOS image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: DeepSeek reduces the stated two-direction case to BIOS downgrade, then proposes the source-style PATCH/POST, generic TaskService polling and FirmwareInventory verification with the host off.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Full PATCH/POST responses, TaskService polling and final FirmwareInventory plus clean host power-on.
deepseek_columns.risk: DeepSeek identifies the destructive BIOS-write and interruption risk.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; the confirmation-gated capability is appropriate, but it narrows upgrade/downgrade to downgrade and assumes an update URI, task model and secure-enough curl usage that the source does not establish.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; correctly rejects embedded credentials, TLS bypass and unverified Redfish semantics, but converts named vendor/project readiness inputs into permanent BLOCKED.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 727/2291 preserves the source Redfish path and FirmwareInventory criterion.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its sequence-896 draft called a destructive firmware update FULLY AUTOMATABLE and is non-counting history, not a decision source.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 permits an approved tool binding with coverage accounting; ED-36 treats images and execution values as readiness; ED-37 prohibits read-only substitution; ED-38 keeps the DUT verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Execute both approved BIOS version directions through a Redfish update path while the host is off and BMC standby remains available, then prove the selected BIOS becomes active and the server satisfies the project-defined configuration, POST and boot acceptance.
original_method: The Master row PATCHes Immediate apply behavior, POSTs a binary BIOS image to a fixed vendor-style URI, waits for unspecified completion, and GETs FirmwareInventory. It embeds a default password in the URL and disables TLS verification; those strings remain source evidence but are not an approved execution recommendation.
manual_activity: An engineer supplies and approves the platform/image/direction contract, secure Redfish method, activation sequence and recovery, and confirms immediately before each write. Once those inputs are frozen, an agent can drive the API and evidence workflow, but it cannot bypass the firmware-change approval gate or issue the final verdict.
required_inputs: board/platform inventory and current, upgrade and downgrade BIOS versions
signed BIOS images, hashes, release notes and intended region/preservation policy
target-advertised Redfish action/URI, payload, apply-time and task/terminal-response contract
protected credentials and trusted management certificate/CA
host-off/BMC-standby, activation/reset/power, settings, POST/OS and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Never execute the literal `root:0penBmc` URLs or `curl -k`; keep credentials out of URLs, command history, process listings and logs, and authenticate the BMC endpoint.
Discover the identified BMC's supported BIOS update action and inventory member; do not assume `/UpdateService/update`, Immediate apply or a TaskService monitor exists.
Verify signed image-to-board and intended-region compatibility before POST; FirmwareInventory labels alone are insufficient target binding.
Keep host-off distinct from AC-removed, preserve BMC standby and stable update power, and run only the approved activation sequence.
On ambiguous HTTP/task status, management loss or failed activation, preserve the first failure and do not retry, reverse direction, reset or power-cycle automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only Redfish capability, inventory, health, task and host-power discovery with redacted authentication; validate images and obtain explicit approval before one transition.
After approval, submit only the advertised vendor action, correlate the exact returned task or synchronous response, and monitor the approved activation/power sequence.
Collect authoritative BIOS version, settings, console POST, OS/kernel, BMC/SEL and management-health evidence; report facts without deciding PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
engineer_actions: Approve each version direction, image/region policy, vendor Redfish contract, secret/TLS method, activation plan and recovery.
Evaluate direction-specific task, BIOS, configuration and boot evidence and assign the final verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its staged API lifecycle fits the function, but it covers downgrade only, inherits an unsafe credential/TLS pattern, assumes generic task polling, and does not establish which FirmwareInventory member is the BIOS target.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the project-approved Redfish BIOS update action discovered from the identified BMC with protected authentication, trusted TLS, signed-image target binding, response-correlated completion handling and an approved activation sequence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source PATCH/POST/GET text, Immediate setting, host-off condition, two directions, linked script and 10/30-minute values remain immutable evidence even when unsafe literals are not executed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Discover the vendor update contract, bind one signed BIOS image and intended regions to the exact board, execute one approved direction, monitor its correlated completion and activation, then independently verify active BIOS, required settings, POST/OS health and logs.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only BMC/BIOS combinations exposing a project-approved Redfish BIOS update service while the host is off and BMC standby is powered.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board, current/target BIOS, BMC, Redfish schema/service, client, CA and recovery-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor Redfish BIOS update, apply-time, activation, preservation and recovery specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the unsafe literal authentication/TLS and assumed URI with a discovered secure service while preserving the Redfish functional path.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Another approved flash tool may satisfy a project BIOS-transition objective but does not prove the source Redfish path; a matching version does not prove every firmware region or setting.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved images, vendor service contract, activation and acceptance plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An HTTP success or FirmwareInventory string can precede failed activation or a nonbootable configuration.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select a different approved update tool, but must record the original Redfish method, actual tool, reason, approval, equivalent checkpoints and the Redfish coverage left unverified. Missing current images or parameters are execution-readiness gaps, not permanent BLOCKED.
expected_evidence: approved platform, BIOS version-direction and region matrix with image hashes/signatures
read-only service root, UpdateService action, apply-time, target-inventory and completion-contract discovery
host-off/BMC-standby, stable-power, settings and health baseline
redacted authenticated request/response plus exact correlated task or synchronous terminal response
post-activation BIOS version, required settings, console POST, OS/kernel, BMC/SEL and management health
tested recovery readiness and separate engineer verdict for each direction

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target BIOS through Redfish with the host initially off. Unsafe credentials/TLS, an assumed URI and incomplete completion semantics are correctable source-method defects; the missing project values do not create competing test purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The BIOS target, two directions, Redfish method and intended outcome are identifiable. A vendor-approved action contract, secure credentials, images, activation criteria and recovery can be supplied as named readiness inputs, so the case is confirmation-gated rather than permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps its PARTIAL-equivalent package/approval class and destructive-risk warning, restores the omitted upgrade direction, and corrects endpoint, task, target-inventory, secret and TLS assumptions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its security, POST and recovery controls but changes permanent BLOCKED because each missing element is an obtainable vendor/project execution contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects its FULLY AUTOMATABLE label because firmware images and explicit destructive approval are mandatory even when API mechanics are scriptable.

review_improvement: Turns the unsafe fixed curl text into a secure, capability-discovered execution contract while preserving the original Redfish coverage and separating task completion, BIOS activation and platform boot evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row has a software-addressable core, but capability does not remove its signed-image, destructive-write and activation approvals. Redfish discovery can resolve the vendor URI and completion model without changing the test purpose, so BLOCKED is too strong. Conversely, firmware-change rules prevent FULLY AUTOMATABLE; REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION accurately captures the ready-to-bind workflow.
